segments: Version scope: The examples below retain the tutorial's NixOS 24.05 context; that release is no longer maintained. Real projects should choose a supported release, pin the nixpkgs revision, and verify the corresponding options. system.stateVersion specifies a compatibility baseline and should not be changed mechanically with each upgrade. The commands in this article are teaching examples and have not been run or verified on a target system.
Translated from nix.dev: Provisioning remote machines via SSH
Deploy NixOS to remote servers over SSH to implement infrastructure as code.
A target server with NixOS already installed
Ensure SSH is enabled on the remote server:

The target must already have NixOS installed, and the deployment configuration should also import that target's hardware-configuration.nix, filesystem configuration, and boot modules. The service fragment here is not a complete bare-metal configuration. First keep a working SSH session and console recovery path available, and confirm that the deploy user can elevate to root. The 24.05 rebuild uses --use-remote-sudo; the equivalent in newer rebuild-ng versions may be --sudo. Consult the target tool's --help.

Build first, then test. test modifies the running system but does not make it the default for the next boot. switch both activates the configuration and updates the system generation/boot configuration.
--build-host: specifies a remote build host; when omitted, builds normally run locally. Do not assume that the special value localhost behaves consistently across versions.

--use-remote-sudo: enables remote sudo for a non-root target user in the historical rebuild implementation. Whether a password can be entered interactively depends on the tool version and connection method.
Deploying Multiple Servers in a Batch

The following script actually activates servers one at a time. Each nixosConfigurations key must exactly match its corresponding name in the array. Complete build/test and SSH verification on a single node before approving the full list. A failure stops subsequent deployments; nodes already deployed successfully are not automatically rolled back as a group. Create deploy.sh:
deploy-rs is a community-maintained deployment tool with support for atomic deployment and rollback.

The attrset below should be the flake's deploy output, with self and the deploy-rs input in scope. Simply saving it as an isolated file does not integrate it with the tool. Also consider exposing deploy-rs.lib.<system>.deployChecks self.deploy under checks. Atomic profile switching, rollback on failure, and magic rollback all depend on configuration and SSH recovery conditions; they do not replace data backups.

Do not put plaintext secrets in Nix strings, the store, images, or Terraform state. agenix-encrypted files can be managed alongside configuration, while private keys remain at controlled paths on the target. Applications read the decrypted files at runtime.

services.myapp is an illustrative interface and must be defined by a real application module; the owner/group must also already exist. Pass the agenix input into the module through specialArgs or an equivalent mechanism.

This is an actual deployment workflow: a push triggers changes on the remote system. Production environments should use protected deployment environments/approvals and least privilege, with third-party actions pinned to verified commit SHAs. Installing Nix does not guarantee that the runner has nixos-rebuild; supply the appropriate version through a pinned tool environment. Prepopulate known_hosts after verifying it through an independent trusted channel. An ad hoc ssh-keyscan only collects candidate public keys; it does not establish trust in the server's identity.
